Your friend is being unreasonable. Uninviting someone from a wedding over heels, especially knowing your financial and mental health situation, is an extreme reaction. A true best friend would have said "wear whatever comfortable shoes you can find" and moved on. The fact that the MOH already stepped up to buy the shawl shows others understood your situation - why couldn't she?

That said, I want to gently push back on something. You have a mother who is covering your finances. I understand your relationship is strained, but asking her for help with a specific item for a wedding isn't disrespectful - it's practical. Pride and difficult relationships sometimes have to take a backseat to reality. You could have framed it as a loan.

The mental health struggles are real and valid and I don't dismiss them at all. Five months waiting for proper support while on antipsychotics and antidepressants and feeling out of control is genuinely hard. But I also think sometimes when we're struggling we can lose track of how our situation looks from the outside to people who don't fully understand mental illness.

However - uninviting you a month before the wedding over shoes after everything you've been through together is cruel and disproportionate. If she can't show you grace during one of the hardest periods of your life, that says more about her than you.
